Thumbtack helps millions of people confidently care for their homes.
Thumbtack is the one app you need to take care of and improve your home — from personalized guidance to AI tools and a best-in-class hiring experience. Every day in every county of the U.S., people turn to Thumbtack to complete urgent repairs, seasonal maintenance and bigger improvements.

We help homeowners know which projects to do, when to do them and who to hire from our growing community of 300,000 local service businesses. If making an impact inspires you, join us. Imagine what we’ll build together.
About the Machine Learning Infrastructure Team
At Thumbtack, our challenges span a wide range of areas, including search, recommendations, matchmaking, pricing, safety, content generation, fraud detection, and more. The ML Infrastructure team is responsible for centralizing, standardizing and evolving AI/ML infrastructure that enables these experiences.

We empower product engineering teams by providing scalable, high-performance systems that drive AI innovation at scale. To read more about some of the engineering challenges at Thumbtack, visit our engineering blog .
Challenge
As a Software Engineer on the ML Infrastructure team, you will work closely with product and platform engineering teams to build and evolve core AI platform capabilities. You will help design and improve systems that allow teams to develop, run, and scale GenAI-powered applications in production. Your work will directly support AI-driven experiences used by millions of customers and pros across the Thumbtack ecosystem.

Build and evolve core AI platform capabilities that enable teams to develop, run, and scale GenAI-powered applications across Thumbtack.
Contribute to the design, development, and deployment of scalable tools and infrastructure to support the efforts of our applied scientists, including traditional ML model training and serving systems, feature and data workflows, CI/CD, orchestration, deployment, and evaluation tooling.
Work hands on across the stack, from backend services and execution infrastructure to integrations with AI models and tooling.
Partner with senior engineers to evaluate next-generation AI infrastructure frameworks and tools that help product teams harness advances in AI.
Drive projects to completion with a strong focus on business impact and measurable outcomes.
Solve complex technical problems and stay up to date with advances in this rapidly evolving space.
In order to be successful, you must bring
1 to 3 years of professional software engineering experience.
Strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and software design.
Proficiency in at least one major programming language, and the ability to work across multiple languages. Our primary stack includes Go and Python.
Experience working with relational or NoSQL databases such as Postgres or DynamoDB.
Demonstrated ability to use AI coding tools in day-to-day workflows and validate, critique, and refine AI-generated output
Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment with a certain level of ambiguity, especially when learning and picking up new technologies when projects require it.
You operate with a bias to action, quickly learning what is needed and taking decisive steps to move work forward in ambiguous, fast-paced environments.

As a Software Engineer on the Firmware team, you will own the software integration, performance, optimization, and debugging of our TCU (Telematics Control Unit).

Managing a complex architecture that integrates third-party hardware with our autonomous vehicle platform, you will analyze diagnostics and log outputs across cellular networks, 4G/5G modems, internal software layers, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth.

You will not only reactively troubleshoot complex field issues but also proactively architect and develop robust host-side connectivity software to handle cellular edge cases and vulnerabilities before they impact operations.
Your work will directly safeguard the safety, reliability, and scaling of the Zoox autonomous fleet. Robust, low-latency connectivity is fundamental to autonomous vehicle deployment, powering essential real-time cloud services, fleet management pipelines, and teleoperation capabilities.

By ensuring our vehicles maintain seamless, high-performance connections under the most demanding real-world conditions, you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge hardware, cloud infrastructure, and test systems to enable Zoox to deliver the future of autonomous mobility.
You will leverage a profound understanding of how these stacks operate to define the architecture, utilize vendor interfaces, and debug complex cross-layer issues.

Contribute and Develop: Contribute to Zoox's firmware and cellular wireless connectivity stack (LTE/5G), developing and enhancing connectivity features across multiple generations of hardware.
Vendor Integration: Act as the primary technical expert working with cellular chipset vendors (e.g., Qualcomm) to integrate their proprietary firmware, SW stacks, and L1-L3 implementations into our custom embedded Linux platform.
Architecture Definition: Define, architect, and validate the critical software interfaces between the RF-baseband, the vendor's protocol stack (AP), and our host system, writing the host-side glue code (C/C++) needed for the Linux networking stack.
Prototyping: Prototype and evaluate next-generation wireless platforms for future Zoox products.
Telemetry and Analytics: Develop the telemetry and analytics platform enabling data collection, analysis, and visualization of data reported from the Zoox fleet.
Investigate and Solve: Investigate and root-cause issues reported by QA teams and customer feedback. Differentiate between host-side bugs and vendor firmware issues using your deep knowledge of cellular protocols.
Quality and Automation: Support test automation frameworks, collaborate with QA, manufacturing, and other software teams, and drive continuous improvements and best practices within the broader organization.

More than 10+ years of experience in embedded linux systems and cellular/wireless stack software/firmware development.
B.S. or M.S. degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience.
Exceptional programming skills in C/C++, Linux OS, and Python/Shell scripting.
Deep architectural understanding of LTE/5G Protocol Stacks (NAS, PDCP, RRC, RLC, MAC, PHY) and 3GPP specifications.
Proven experience successfully integrating third-party cellular modems and proprietary stacks, with hands-on experience using Qualcomm ecosystems and cellular network analysis tools (e.g., QXDM , Shannon Tools, Wireshark).
Good understanding of Embedded Systems, OS concepts, computer architecture, data structures, and algorithms.
Hands-on experience in maintaining the Linux Applications, kernel code and embedded services, including experience porting and patching open-source packages within the Yocto Project environment.
Strong understanding of networking concepts (Ethernet, TCP/IP, IP routing design, VLANs, firewalls, and both IPv4 and IPv6 protocols).

Working experience in the Automotive industry.
Familiarity with other wireless technologies (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, BLE).
Familiarity with embedded interfaces (UART, I2C, I2S, SPI, CAN, PCIe, etc.).
Prior experience collaborating with test teams using industry-standard network emulation tools (e.g., Keysight UXM).
Experience in design, develop, and secure wireless software systems by implementing robust network protocols and advanced wireless security protocols.
Highly motivated and self-directed. Thrives in a collaborative environment and can clearly communicate complex technical issues to both internal teams and external vendors.

About Warp
Warp is the AI-native Employee Management Platform for ambitious companies. Our platform includes HRIS, payroll, IT, benefits, tax compliance, and more - all built from scratch on an AI-native architecture from day 1.
Warp embeds itself into every part of a company's people operating layer, we process over half a billion $ annually in payroll, on track to grow to $2B.
Legacy vendors in our space built their businesses by profiting from complexity. Warp is built from day one for AI to be the primary operator, not a feature. Every advance in LLM capability widens our lead.
We hire people who ship constantly, own outcomes, and care about craft. If you want to build something that automates an entire category of core work, not just another point solution, this is the place.
We've raised over $85M from top investors like Ashton Kutcher/Sound Ventures, Y Combinator, founders of Dropbox, Replit, SV Angel, and Homebrew Capital. Built by an obsessive team from MIT, Ramp, Brex, Google, Dropbox, Apple, and more.

As a Software Engineer on the Product team, you'll build the features that make Warp indispensable. This isn't a siloed frontend or backend role. You'll work full-stack across our entire product surface, interface directly with customers, spec features alongside the team, and ship things that matter. One week you're building HRIS workflows, the next you're wiring up an AI agent that automates something a customer used to do manually.

Build and own product features across Warp's full surface: HRIS, payroll, benefits, IT, Warp AI agents, and more
Work full-stack: schema design, backend services, and polished frontends
Interface directly with customers and the sales team to understand pain points and turn them into product
Collaborate directly with the CTO and CEO
Help us scale 10x in the next year

Love programming and obsess over details

Have shipped features that real users rely on

High agency. You figure things out.

Join the Sleep Fitness Movement
At Eight Sleep, we're on a mission to fuel human potential through optimal sleep. As the world's first sleep fitness company, we're redefining what it means to be well-rested and building the most advanced hardware, software, and AI technology to make it possible. Our products power peak mental, physical, and emotional performance by transforming every night of sleep into a personalized, data-driven recovery experience.
Every role at Eight Sleep is a chance to create cutting-edge technology, collaborate with world-class talent, and help shape a future where sleep isn't passive, it's a powerful tool for living better. If you're tired of the ordinary and driven to build at the edge of what's possible, this is your moment.
High Standards. No Apologies.
We operate with intensity because our mission demands it. At Eight Sleep, we bring the same mindset as the world's top performers: focused, relentless, and always pushing to be in the top 1% of our craft. This isn't a 9-to-5. Our team is deeply committed, often putting in the extra effort, not because we're told to, but because we're invested in building something category-defining.

We're hiring a Software Engineer to help us move fast on eightsleep.com . You'll work closely with the growth, marketing, and design teams to ship landing pages, run a high volume of A/B tests, and keep our analytics and conversion funnels sharp on a high-traffic storefront serving customers around the world.
This is a hands-on, high-velocity role. If you like turning ideas into shipped, measurable experiments, and seeing your work go live within days, you'll feel at home here.
How you’ll contribute
Build marketing pages. Ship landing pages, campaign pages, and partner/influencer pages, translating designs into clean, responsive, accessible components.
Run experiments end-to-end. Design, build, and launch A/B tests; instrument the funnels you need, then read the results and share what you learn. Bring your own test ideas to the table.
Build scalable, templatized systems that make launching new pages efficient and consistent.
Own the analytics stack. Maintain and extend our tracking and advertising integrations, and keep event data accurate and privacy-compliant.
Optimize conversion. Improve every step of the funnel: promos, email capture, CTAs, messaging, and page performance.
Own SEO and accessibility. Keep metadata, sitemaps, structured data, and page speed in great shape, and make sure everything you ship is accessible.
Build for a global audience. Create localized pages and experiments across our supported regions and languages.
What you need to succeed
Strong React and Next.js experience; comfortable across the modern front-end stack and TypeScript.
Experiment-design sense . You can frame a clean hypothesis, think about sample size and significance, and trust a result before acting on it.
5+ years in front-end web development , ideally in growth, marketing, or ecommerce contexts.
Strong attention to detail. You QA your own work and ship things that don't bounce back.
Hands-on with product analytics (Amplitude or similar): funnels, cohorts, and event tracking.
Comfortable with Google Tag Manager and GA4 .
Care for web performance (Core Web Vitals) and accessibility .
Awareness of data privacy / consent requirements and how they affect tracking.
AI built into how you work. You use coding assistants and other AI tools to move faster and raise your output.
A bias toward shipping quickly and iterating.

Experience with SEO/AEO, including structured data.
Internationalization / localization work.
Server-side conversion tracking (CAPI / server-to-server).
Tailwind CSS and design-system component work; Figma-to-code workflows.
Familiarity with a headless CMS and media/asset pipelines.
Experience with media-heavy sites and asset optimization.
How we work
Config-driven and fast. A lot of our growth surface is defined declaratively, so a well-scoped change goes from idea to production in a day, not a sprint. We're experiment-led, we'd rather ship a test and learn than debate. You'll have real ownership over what you build and a direct line to the impact it has.

Creative Full Stack Developer - London based
Experience Design
London
Hybrid

We’re looking for a Full Stack Developer with 3-5 years experience and a genuine interest in AI and creative technology. You’re curious about where creativity and technology are heading, and excited by the chance to help shape what’s next. You enjoy building across the full stack and want to bring that into a creative studio where the ideas are ambitious, the challenges are varied, and experimentation is part of the process.

You’ll sit with designers and strategists, not across a wall from them. You’ll build brands at an independent studio without layers of agency bureaucracy. You won’t sit downstream of the work. You’ll help define what’s possible, then build it.

Who we are.

We are a group of people who make beautiful, original brands that change the world for the better. We’re fuelled by creativity and reject convention. We are trusted by some of the world’s most interesting companies, including Formula 1, TikTok, Hulu, Audible, Roli, ITV X, British Land, ESPN, Channel 4, Eurosport, Netflix and AC Milan. Brands that seek to be brave and challenge convention.

Our studio home is based in London (N1), and we come together at least 3 days a week to enjoy the space, collaborate and time together. Studio time and our wonderful surroundings are very important for creativity to thrive. Working together enables us to approach new ideas and inventions creatively and to enjoy the journey.

We partner with brands and in-house creative teams across the world from our London studio. We seek revolution rather than evolution and embrace change to remain fiercely original.

Great design is born of difference; we constantly seek new perspectives and identities to build our team. We’re a vibrant, eclectic, open group of people from South Korea, Iran, Venezuela and everywhere in between, which makes for a rich environment full of ideas.

How we see technology.

We’re interested in what technology makes possible, not technology for its own sake. Emerging and intelligent tools are changing how brands and systems meet the world. We bring the same care, judgement and invention to that shift as we do to everything else.

Engineering here is craft, not plumbing. It isn’t an executional add-on. It’s a system-level way of building brands and design systems that work everywhere, for everyone. We’re not chasing novelty. We’re building better tools, more useful systems and more meaningful experiences.

We have a view on AI. We think it will become invisible infrastructure, and that systems will increasingly learn to prefer the average. Our bet is on conviction over efficiency. If you’re tired of the hype and want to build with people who have actually thought about it, you’ll feel at home.

Our Stack.

We build in Next.js and React, TypeScript end to end, SCSS Modules for styling, and Convex or Supabase for data and realtime. Much of our interesting brand work lives in the creative-web layer; React Three Fiber, Three.js, GLSL shaders, Motion and increasingly in AI-native builds with the Vercel AI SDK.

You don’t need to have shipped in every one of these. You do need to know at least one part of this stack deeply deeply enough to have opinions, to know why you’d reach for it, and to catch when something’s subtly wrong.

Bonus, not required: Node.js, React Native, Rive, WebGL post-processing, or experience wiring up embeddings, RAG and agent workflows.

You have a strong eye for design and understand that great digital experiences rely on both thoughtful interaction and well-crafted code. You notice when something doesn’t feel quite right and know how to improve it. You’ll prototype, build, test and iterate to bring early-stage ideas to life.

You’re proactive, comfortable with uncertainty and motivated by curiosity. Rather than waiting for direction, you bring ideas, explore possibilities, learn through making and share what you discover along the way.

What you do.

These are just some of the things we’d expect. Brilliance comes in many forms though; our minds are always open.

You write and own code across the full stack, confidently developing front-end and back-end experiences that bring ambitious creative ideas to life.

You read code as carefully as you write it. You work fluently with AI, and you know when not to. Agents and automation are part of how you build but you bring judgement to it. When to reach for a tool, when to write it yourself, and how to tell the difference.

You prototype rapidly, using experimentation and iteration to test ideas and accelerate learning before investing in polished solutions.

You collaborate closely with designers, creative directors and strategists from the earliest stages of a project, contributing technical thinking that helps shape ideas rather than simply delivering them.

You’re comfortable working in ambiguity, embracing evolving briefs and adapting as ideas develop through experimentation, feedback and collaboration.

s.t:
Fanvue is one of the fastest-growing creator monetisation platforms globally. We're an AI-powered, creator-first platform helping creators connect, engage, and earn directly from their audiences at scale. Following our recent Series A, Fanvue has surpassed $200m+ in annual recurring revenue, with triple-digit year-on-year growth, supporting hundreds of thousands of creators and millions of fans worldwide.
Growth engineering at Fanvue exists to move core product metrics fast. It's a small team that reads out experiments every week, and the surface area is enormous: signup, onboarding, activation, referral loops, retention, and the funnels underneath all of them. There is far more worth testing than there are people to test it. This role exists to close that gap.

We're hiring a Full Stack Engineer to work on Fanvue's Growth streams, partnering closely with Product, Design, Data and Marketing to design, ship and iterate on high-impact experiments across acquisition, onboarding, activation and retention.
This is highly execution-focused. You'll be testing ideas in production within your first weeks, not writing specs about them. The team runs on a weekly experiment cadence with real readouts, so the loop between an idea and knowing whether it worked is short, and you own both ends of it.
It suits someone who wants to be judged on whether the metric moved.

Design, build and ship growth experiments across signup, onboarding, activation and retention flows
Own features end to end, from idea through implementation, measurement and iteration
Build and refine growth loops such as referrals, sharing mechanics and viral surfaces
Run A/B and multivariate tests, and read the results honestly, including the ones that kill your own idea
Partner with Product and Design to prioritise and scope what's worth testing
Improve the performance and reliability of growth-critical user journeys
Use analytics and data tooling to guide technical and product decisions
Continuously find and remove friction in creator and fan funnels

Strong full stack engineering experience with a clear bias toward shipping
Comfortable across frontend and backend, and willing to go wherever the problem is
Experienced with modern web stacks such as TypeScript, Node.js, React and relational databases
Familiar with experimentation frameworks, analytics tooling and funnel metrics
Comfortable in ambiguity, with a strong bias toward action
Data-informed and outcome-driven rather than feature-focused
A clear communicator who works well with product, design and growth partners
High ownership, high agency, and an appetite for fast iteration

Experience in the creator economy, consumer subscription, marketplaces or social platforms
Hands-on with Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog or similar
A track record of growth loops you built that are still running
✨ You'll Thrive Here If
You'd rather ship a scrappy test this week than a polished one next quarter
You want to be measured on whether the number moved, not on what you delivered
You're happy to kill your own experiment when the data says so
You go and find the opportunity rather than waiting for it to arrive as a ticket
⚠️ You'll Struggle Here If
You prefer long planning cycles to fast iteration

As a Senior Software Engineer at Form3, you’ll work on established, high-volume services that sit at the heart of Form3’s cloud-native payment platform. These are critical systems where reliability, resilience and operational excellence matter every single day.
This is a role for engineers who enjoy evolving critical systems at scale. You’ll be working on mature, high-volume services where thoughtful design, careful testing, operational discipline and reliability are just as important as delivering new capability.
You’ll solve complex engineering challenges across services that support real-time payment flows, high availability, fault tolerance, security and performance within a microservice architecture. You’ll need to think carefully about how changes are designed, tested, released and operated, balancing delivery speed with the discipline required for mission-critical financial infrastructure.
You’ll work closely with experienced engineers, product teams and operational stakeholders to improve, evolve and run services that customers depend on. This could include enhancing existing payment capabilities, improving service resilience, simplifying complex systems, reducing operational risk, or building new functionality into mature services without compromising stability.

Designing, building, and running cloud-native microservices in Go that are the backbone of our real-time payments platform
Building systems that are highly available, low-latency, and scalable, handling billions of payment requests with precision and resilience
Taking full ownership of services: from initial design and implementation to deployment and production support
Working with a mindset where cost-efficiency, observability, and operational excellence are core to how we build
Collaborating closely with other engineers in a flat, autonomous team structure, with a strong focus on code quality, simplicity, and continuous improvement
Working with modern tooling and technologies such as Golang, Kubernetes, CockroachDB and NATS JetStream in a highly automated DevOps environment

Deep understanding of designing and building distributed systems
Enjoys working on complex challenges within critical software where high performance and robustness are essential
Familiarity with cloud and containerisation technologies, test automation tools and CI/CD pipelines
Interest in owning projects end-to-end and supporting them as they go live in production
Appreciation of clean code and software engineering best-practice
Experience with Go, along with a “right tool for the job” mentality
Great communication skills who enjoy sharing knowledge and collaborating with others

At Form3, our engineering team is the backbone of everything we do. A remote first group of highly skilled, collaborative, and forward-thinking individuals passionate about building secure, scalable, and reliable payment technology. We operate in a true DevOps model, where engineers take full ownership of the software lifecycle, from design and implementation to deployment and operation in production.
We value clean code, automation, simplicity, and continuous improvement. Our engineers work in small, autonomous teams with a flat structure and minimal bureaucracy, promoting a culture of trust, transparency, and accountability. We use modern technologies (Golang, Kubernetes, AWS, and more) and embrace a cloud-native, event-driven architecture to support our microservices platform.
Expect a culture of knowledge sharing, where pull requests are thoughtful conversations, and technical decisions are made collectively and with care. If you're motivated by solving complex problems at scale and enjoy working with other talented engineers who care deeply about doing things right, you'll feel right at home here.

Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.
Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.
We’re already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $500m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.
Why we’re hiring
We're post-PMF and revenue generating, launching in the US ahead of a Series A. Early enough that you'll shape how engineering works here, late enough that you're not gambling on whether the product works.
You'll own significant parts of the product and ship the things customers feel most. It's a regulated platform moving money across multiple jurisdictions, so the work has to be right and it still has to be fast.
We also want the bar to move while you're here. Senior engineers set the standard through the quality of what they ship, how they review, and the problems they choose to fix rather than work around.
Alongside that, we're rethinking how we build with AI. We use the tools, but we know there's a step change available to teams who redesign their whole workflow around them rather than adding AI to how they already work. If you've already done that somewhere else, you'll have a lot of room here.

You've built and run non-trivial production systems, and you've learned what works in which situations rather than defaulting to one approach.
Strong architectural judgement. Most of our code is now written by an LLM, which means you need to own the decisions around it: how the system is structured, what the patterns are, whether the thing being built is the right thing at all. Our stack is Go, and if you learn quickly, not having written it isn't a problem.
A serious AI practice. You can talk specifically about how AI has changed the way you build, what it's actually made faster, and what you've shared with the teams you've worked in.
Directness. You give feedback when something isn't good enough and take it just as well.
Good instincts about what's worth doing. You know when something needs to be built properly and when it doesn't, and you push for the work that makes everyone around you faster.
Probably not for you if
You think the impact of AI on engineering is overstated. You'd rather be handed a fully specified ticket than question the brief. Or the learning curve across finance, compliance and multiple jurisdictions sounds like a chore rather than the interesting part.
The people who do well here find that last bit genuinely interesting. Understanding how capital actually moves, and what the rules allow in each jurisdiction, is most of what makes this product hard to build and hard to copy.
The hiring process
Three stages, usually inside two weeks, with detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one.
Call with Imani, our Head of People and Talent . You'll get a proper picture of the role and the company, and we'll get into how you work and how you build.
System design session with our engineering team . No leetcode and no take-home. We want to see how you approach a problem and structure a solution.
Paid trial day. A real Odin problem with everything you need handed to you. You see how we work, we see how you ship.
Working at Odin
Two setups work for this role: London hybrid (three days a week in the office) or remote from elsewhere in Europe with quarterly trips to London.

Wir sind Feinheit: eine holokratisch geführte Kommunikations- und Webagentur mit Standorten in Zürich und Bern und rund 20 Mitarbeitenden. Seit 2006 entwickeln wir Kommunikationslösungen und digitale Werkzeuge für Projekte, die der Welt gut tun. Als Mitglied der Leading Swiss Agencies gehören wir zu den führenden Agenturen der Schweiz.

Per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung suchen wir als Ergänzung für unser Team eine:n

Senior Full-Stack Entwickler:in

Dein Pensum: 70-100%

Dein Arbeitsort: Zürich, mit der Möglichkeit für Home Office. Unser technisches Team arbeitet vor Ort, deshalb ist regelmässige Anwesenheit in Zürich erwünscht. Home Office (und Bern) ist möglich.

Das wirst du bei Feinheit tun

Du programmierst neue Websites und Webapplikationen – vom Backend (Python, Django) über die Datenbank bis ins Frontend (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).

Du überwachst während der Arbeitszeit den Betrieb unserer Websites. Fehlermeldungen behältst du im Blick, reagierst selbst auf auftretende Fehler und eskalierst, wenn nötig.

Du bringst deine technische Expertise in der Problemlösung ein – intern im Projektteam und extern gegenüber der Kundschaft.

Du entwickelst unsere IT-Infrastruktur mit, insbesondere die Hosting- und Monitoring-Umgebung.

Das bringst du mit

Damit du bei uns durchstartest, solltest du das Folgende auf jeden Fall mitbringen:

Fundierte Erfahrung in der Webentwicklung – sowohl im Backend wie auch im Frontend.

Solide Backend-Kenntnisse in einer modernen Programmiersprache (idealerweise Python) sowie Verständnis für Datenbanken (SQL).

Vertrautheit mit Unix-/Linux-Systemen, die Arbeit auf der Kommandozeile ist für dich selbstverständlicher Alltag.

Echtes Interesse und Freude am Frontend (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, moderne Frameworks). Hier willst du mehr als nur mithalten.

Die Bereitschaft, Verantwortung für Betrieb und Monitoring zu übernehmen: Fehler früh erkennen, selbst beheben oder gezielt eskalieren.

Neugierde und Lust am Lernen. Im KI-Zeitalter eignet man sich neue Werkzeuge und Frameworks schnell an – das siehst du als Chance.

Analytisch-konzeptionelles Denken, starke Eigeninitiative sowie eine lösungs- und dienstleistungsorientierte Arbeitsweise.

Gerne Agentur- oder Start-Up-Erfahrung.

Konkrete Erfahrung mit Django, unserem Haupt-Framework. Falls nicht: Wer die Grundlagen mitbringt, arbeitet sich bei uns schnell ein.

Erfahrung mit (p)react oder einem anderen modernen SPA-Framework.

Erfahrung mit Error-Monitoring-Tools wie Sentry.

Kenntnisse in Hosting, Deployment und CI/CD.

Darauf kannst du dich freuen

Dein Alltag ist durch die Zusammenarbeit mit unterschiedlichen Organisationen auf Seite der Auftraggeberschaft abwechslungsreich: Wir arbeiten für NGO, politische Organisationen, öffentliche Institutionen, KMU sowie Kultur- und Bildungsinstitutionen.

Durch unser Angebot massgeschneiderter Web-Lösungen bringt jedes Projektsetting neue Aufgaben mit sich.

In unserem holokratischen Organisationsmodell hast du grosse Einflussmöglichkeiten hinsichtlich der Governance, deiner Aufgaben und der Zusammenarbeit im gesamten Team.

Wir sind überzeugt, dass eine interdisziplinäre und selbstorganisierte Zusammenarbeit auf Augenhöhe nicht nur zu den besten Ergebnissen in einem Projekt, sondern auch zu einem guten Teamspirit beiträgt. Mit derselben Überzeugung streben wir eine diverse Teamzusammensetzung an und achten beispielsweise auf ausgeglichene Geschlechterverhältnisse.

At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

HDR is a Top 10 Architectural & Engineering (A&E) firm in the United States as ranked by Engineering News Record and is also one of the largest employee-owned A&E companies in the United States.

HDR has been selected to run the Installation Engineering and Installation Management functions of the Civil Engineer Squadron for the United Stated Air Force Academy (USAFA). As such, we will be placing a multi-disciplinary A&E team of 50+ professionals at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs.

The contract is expected to begin in early 2026 and covers an eight-year period from 2026 through 2034. The U.S. Air Force Academy is one of the premier universities in our country and is one of the most widely visited locations in all of Colorado.

The Air Force Academy has a rich history and a unique mission to educate and train future Air Force leaders. HDR is honored to be selected for these components of the of the Base Maintenance Contract (BMC) in conjunction with Tessera, who will be running and leading the master contract with the Air Force.

HDR will be performing wide-ranging facility management services to include but not limited to: planning, programming, design, asset management, construction inspection, energy management, real estate, environmental, cultural resources, space planning, CAD, GIS, cost estimating, and numerous other functions.

Ideal candidates will have knowledge and/or experience with federal contracts and/or the Air Force Civil Engineering Squadron. They will also have a strong enthusiasm to ensure the cadets and future Air Force Leaders live and learn in state-of-the-art facilities and have the necessary resources to serve our country to the best of their abilities.

This position is full time and located on-site at the USAFA.

In the role of Programmer Lead your duties are predominantly intellectual in nature and vary depending on each project’s needs. The position requires discretion and judgment based upon knowledge of Unified Facilities Criteria, Air Force Programming requirements e.g. DAFMAN 32-1084 and Air Force Institute of Technology programming course instruction e.g. WMGT 423. We'll count on you to:

Be responsible for managing the Facility AMP and coordinate project authorizations independently, reflecting a leadership role within the installation planning team.

Lean on your deep technical knowledge of AFI 32-1032 and AFI 32-1023 for planning and programming appropriated fund maintenance, repair, and construction projects for garnering funding from higher headquarters.

Have a deep understanding of the facility programming process to articulate the requirements and benefits of each project to the Air Force as well as any adverse impacts not approving a project may have.

Identify project requirements (define project scopes) to satisfy current and future mission needs.
Provide advice and assistance to the Engineering Flight in writing, coordinating, and processing DOD Form 1391s in support of Facility Sustainment Restoration Modernization (FSRM) and Military Construction (MILCON) projects.
Manage the development of 1391's, threshold reporting and compliance with AFI's.
Develop rough order of magnitude (ROM) construction cost estimates utilizing government provided software (similar to RS Means).
Be responsible for a wide range of detailed deliverables including justifications, space requirement calculations, site plans, coordination with HHQ authorization tools, and the integration of funding timelines with construction schedules.
Provide advice in development of the Base Comprehensive Asset Management Plan (BCAMP).
Provide advice with documenting requirements and acquiring both the authority and resources necessary to accomplish the work.
Provide advice with obtaining and verifying information to justify and gain Congressional funding approval.
Provide advice in support of working with Civil Engineering Operations Flight and other USAFA mission partners through asset management to develop requirements.
Provide advice in support of generating documentation in pre-acquisition efforts for FSRM and MILCON projects.
Develop and submit project lists (e.g., BCAMP, MILCON, Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC), Energy Resilience and Conservation Investment Program (ERCIP), etc.).

A minimum of 3 years Air Force Civil Engineering Squadron programming experience
Ability to work in person and on site at United States Air Force Academy
Ability to pass a background check
Knowledge of the Unified Facilities Criteria
Completion of AFIT training courses WMGT 331, 417 & 423, WENG 400 & 500
Due to client contract requirements, US Citizenship - US Naturalized citizen is required
This position is subject to a governmental background check

Bachelor's degree in related fields (preferably engineering, architecture, or construction)
A minimum of 10 years experience in the Architecture/Engineering/Construction industry
Ability to interact and work alongside daily with various stakeholders
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to submit and pass a background check
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

Optimize performance, memory usage, and throughput of PHY software components
Verification, Testing, and Debug

Debug complex PHY, timing, RF, and performance issues across software and hardware boundaries
Technical Leadership and Delivery

Support customer requests related to 5G PHY features and performance
Document PHY designs, implementations, and results in Confluence or equivalent systems
Collaboration and Ways of Working
Collaborate with RF, systems, hardware, and protocol stack teams to ensure clean PHY-MAC interfaces
Work effectively in a global, distributed team across Europe, India, and the U.S.
Follow SCRUM / Agile and Continuous Integration development practices
Operate autonomously while maintaining strong technical communication

Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. The Superhuman suite of apps and agents brings AI wherever people work, integrating with over 1 million applications and websites.

The company’s products include Grammarly’s writing assistance, Superhuman Docs’ collaborative workspaces, Mail’s inbox management, and Go, the proactive AI assistant that understands context and delivers help automatically.

We're looking for a Back-End Software Engineer who wants to build ambitious AI features and own them end-to-end, from idea to production.

At the same time, this is not a narrowly defined back-end position.

The right person is comfortable moving across the stack when the product demands it—whether that means working on a client platform, a shared protocol, or the infrastructure needed to bring a feature to life.

Superhuman's engineers and researchers have the freedom to innovate and uncover breakthroughs—and, in turn, influence our product roadmap. The complexity of our technical challenges is growing rapidly as we scale our interfaces, algorithms, and infrastructure. You can hear more from our team on our technical blog.

Prototyping with standards. We ship fast, but not at all costs. Prototypes have tests, clean APIs, and documentation.

Know Your Rights.

Insurance is one of the world's largest industries and one of the most painful to interact with . Paper forms. Sluggish call centres. Three-week underwriting cycles. Claims that vanish into queues. We are rebuilding all of it on top of a modern platform and AI agents that actually do the work, not pretend to.
You will not be picking up tickets. You will be deciding what to build, prototyping it on Monday, shipping a draft to a real customer by Friday, and improving it from real usage. We expect you to push the product, the codebase, and the way we work.
Why This Role Exists
We are looking for someone who treats AI as a creative material, not a feature on a roadmap. The next year of insurance is being defined right now. What gets automated, what gets reimagined, what gets thrown out. We want builders who want to be in that room and ship the answer.
The team is small. The mandate is large. If your highest-energy work has historically come from solving real problems end to end, this is the seat.

Own outcomes, not tickets. Pick the biggest lever for our customers each sprint and drive it to live. Surface the next one yourself.
Build with AI as a primary tool, not a chatbot bolt-on. OCR, document understanding, generation, agent loops, evaluation harnesses. You decide where each fits.
Ship prototypes fast, then make them production-grade. A working demo on day three beats a perfect plan on day ten.
Work directly with customers. You will see real claims, real underwriting screens, real broker workflows. You will watch users hit dead ends and decide what to fix.
Raise the bar on the codebase. Reviews, refactors, testability, observability. Not as policy, as habit.
Push the team forward. Skills, agents, internal tools, engineering standards. Propose them, build them, get them adopted.

You ship. Ideas without execution do not count for you.
High agency. You do not wait for a card to be assigned. You see what is worth doing and you start.
Strong opinions, loosely held. You make calls with incomplete information and change your mind when the evidence shifts.
Curious about the domain. Insurance is messy and full of weird incentives. That intrigues you, not annoys you.
Fluent with AI. You have shipped something real with LLMs or agents. You know where the magic ends and where you have to engineer carefully.
Care about humans on the other end. Insurance done right gives people peace of mind in their worst weeks. That is the point.
Your Toolbox
We use Node.js + TypeScript + Nest.js on the back end, Vue (and some React) on the front end, GraphQL, MongoDB, Docker, AWS. AI work spans OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, plus a growing set of in-house skills and agents. You do not need to have used every piece. You do need to be the kind of engineer who picks up a new tool and is shipping with it within the week.
What We Expect at This Level
6+ years building production systems. Track record of complex, customer-facing software shipped, not just maintained.
Real AI experience. You have built and shipped at least one substantive AI-driven feature. POCs that died in a notebook do not count here.
Strong fundamentals. OO, design patterns, testing, web security, performance. You do not need a refresher.
Cloud comfort. AWS, Azure, or GCP. At least one in depth, the rest enough to hold a conversation.
Communication. You can explain a tradeoff to a non-technical stakeholder in two minutes and to an engineer in one.

s.h: Not Suitable for the Role If…

You prefer tickets assigned to you over choosing what to build.
You measure your work in lines of code, not outcomes.
You see AI as a buzzword to put on your CV rather than a tool you have actually used in anger.
You want a process-heavy environment with detailed specs handed down from product.

Design, build, and ship full-stack features end-to-end — UI, APIs, business logic, data models, and integrations — with a strong bias for clean, maintainable, well-tested code.

Own features through the full lifecycle: solution design, development, testing, deployment, and production support.
Contribute to CI/CD, automated testing, code reviews, and Agile ceremonies; and raise the bar on engineering practices across the team.

Scopely Explore (formerly known as Niantic) seeks a Software Engineer to design and build the data infrastructure and experimentation platforms that power our mobile games. You will develop systems that help game, product, analytics, and engineering teams run trustworthy experiments, understand player behavior, and make better decisions at scale.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will write production code, make foundational architectural decisions, and operate critical distributed systems while guiding the technical direction of the platform.

Beyond individual technical contribution, you will help lead and grow the Data Infrastructure organization by aligning engineers and cross-functional partners, mentoring engineers, and driving multi-team initiatives from strategy through delivery.

Depending on team structure and business needs, this role may also include formal people-management responsibilities. We seek creative engineers with excellent technical judgment, strong interpersonal skills, and an eagerness to embrace new technologies and AI-native development methodologies.

Do you want to build the foundations that enable faster learning and better player experiences across Scopely Explore?

You design, build, and operate scalable data infrastructure and experimentation systems for both general product experimentation and game-specific use cases.
You lead the technical design of capabilities such as experiment assignment, player segmentation, exposure logging, telemetry processing, metric computation, guardrails, and reproducible analysis.
You build reliable batch and streaming data pipelines using technologies such as Apache Beam, Apache Spark, Ray, Apache Flink, and Apache Kafka.
You design data platforms on GCP using technologies such as BigQuery, Apache Iceberg, Google Cloud Storage, Kubernetes, Airflow, and Terraform.
You remain hands-on throughout the development lifecycle, contributing production code and solving complex problems in distributed computing, streaming, orchestration, and storage.
You develop effective methodologies and guardrails for AI-assisted and agentic engineering, including context management, automated validation, evaluations, human review, and responsible adoption.
You use AI-native workflows across your end-to-end responsibilities, including architecture exploration, implementation, testing, code review, documentation, debugging, incident response, and platform operations.
You maintain ownership of the correctness, security, performance, and maintainability of all work produced with AI assistance.
You evaluate new technologies pragmatically and apply them where they materially improve engineering velocity, platform reliability, or experimentation quality.
You lead the technical direction and delivery of the Data Infrastructure, aligning engineers and cross-functional partners around shared priorities, architectural decisions, trade-offs, and multi-quarter execution plans.
You coach and develop engineers through mentorship, actionable feedback, and technical guidance, while fostering a collaborative, high-performing team culture and remaining hands-on in architecture and critical implementation.

You have a demonstrated ability to use AI-native workflows across the full engineering lifecycle while independently evaluating and validating their output.
You have extensive experience designing, building, and operating production data platforms or other large-scale distributed systems.
You demonstrate strong programming ability in one or more of Java, Python, Go, or Rust. Experience with Java or Python is especially relevant to this role.
You have deep experience with cloud data infrastructure, preferably GCP and BigQuery.
You understand distributed computing and have production experience with frameworks such as Apache Beam, Apache Spark, or Ray.
You have experience building real-time data systems with technologies such as Apache Flink, Apache Kafka, or comparable streaming frameworks.
You have experience with orchestration, container, and infrastructure automation technologies such as Kubernetes, Airflow, and Terraform.
You understand modern storage and lakehouse architectures, including technologies such as Apache Iceberg and object storage systems such as Google Cloud Storage.
You have experience building experimentation, analytics, telemetry, or data products used by multiple engineering and product teams.
You understand the foundations of trustworthy experimentation, including assignment, exposure tracking, metric definition, data quality, reproducibility, and statistical interpretation.
You have experience defining technical direction and driving complex, cross-team initiatives while remaining directly involved in implementation.
Demonstrated history of leading delivery of complex projects involving multiple engineers and cross-functional partners, from strategy and planning through launch and operational ownership.
Experience managing and developing engineering teams, including hiring, performance feedback, career growth, and fostering an effective, inclusive team culture.
You communicate clearly and work effectively with distributed, cross-functional teams.
You are proficient in English. Japanese proficiency is a bonus.

Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others.

Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.

**Erfahrung: **Umfassende Erfahrung im Aufbau und Betrieb cloud-nativer Plattformen sowie im Einsatz moderner Open-Source-AI-Toolstacks. Sie sind versiert in der Entwicklung, Integration und produktiven Überführung KI-basierter Anwendungen und Services.

C++/Kotlin Software Developer (RustRover Debugger)
You care deeply about how developer tools are built, especially when it comes to the intricacies of debugging. You enjoy solving complex, low-level problems and want to make the Rust ecosystem better for everyone.
About JetBrains
We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

Rust is growing fast. To give the community a dedicated, smart IDE, we released RustRover, a core part of which is the debugger. Right now, it sets a high bar, but there's plenty of room to push it further – both by building new features and by untangling tricky configurations.
As a Software Developer on the RustRover team, you’ll take ownership of the RustRover debugger's state, driving its development across two interconnected parts: the OS-specific C++ debugger (LLDB or GDB) and the IntelliJ-based Java/Kotlin client. You’ll work independently but collaborate closely with our flat, cross-functional team of developers, QA specialists, and support engineers to make debugging Rust applications smoother and more reliable.

Improve and expand the RustRover debugger across its C++ backend and Java/Kotlin frontend.
Implement new IDE run/debug configurations, such as remote development support.
Enhance Rust expression evaluation capabilities.
Investigate and fix OS-specific SIGSEGV errors in C++ code from LLDB.
Design clear, maintainable code and ensure the algorithms behind it are sound.

A genuine interest in making development and debugging more convenient.
Comfort taking ownership of complex problems and figuring things out.
An appreciation for clean, readable, and maintainable code.
A proactive approach to communication and the ability to work independently.
Openness to diverse opinions and the ability to explain your reasoning clearly.
A drive to master new approaches, technologies, and paradigms.
What you’ll need
Strong proficiency in C++ programming.
A solid understanding of system programming and multi-process communication.
A strong grasp of software development processes and life cycles.
Basic knowledge of Java or Kotlin, or a readiness to learn quickly.
Familiarity with compiler development, LLVM/LLDB, or low-level debugging on various OS platforms is a strong plus.
Experience with other languages like Rust, Clojure, Python, Ruby, or Haskell is also a plus.
What success looks like
Success in this role means you're independently driving improvements in the RustRover debugger, bridging the gap between the C++ backend and the Kotlin/Java client. You are actively solving complex configuration issues, introducing reliable new features, and leaving the codebase cleaner than you found it. Ultimately, you are earning the trust of the Rust community by making their debugging experience significantly smoother.

s.h: Este rol NO es para ti si
s.t:
Prefieres que te lleguen las tareas ya definidas. Tu TL te va a decir qué hay que lograr, no cómo. Escalas lo que esté fuera de tu alcance; el resto lo resuelves tú.
Quieres quedarte solo en el front. El onboarding vive en React y se apoya en servicios en Python: te vas a meter en los dos lados.

+6 años desarrollando software y experiencia demostrable como fullstack, idealmente con stack Python.
Manejo real de React. No pedimos que seas el referente del equipo: sí que puedas discutir de igual a igual una decisión de arquitectura de front y sostenerla con argumentos.
Experiencia modelando flujos de negocio multi-paso : máquinas de estado, pasos con precondiciones, reintentos, procesos que se abandonan y se retoman días después.
Disposición y foco sobre estabilidad, escalabilidad y buenas prácticas , incluidas estrategias de testing (unitario, integración y E2E) sobre flujos críticos, con simulación de servicios de terceros.
Criterio de producto. Sabes leer una métrica de caída, hablar con quien atiende al cliente y decidir qué se arregla primero. Discutes el requerimiento antes de implementarlo.
Autonomía real y comunicación asertiva : capacidad de influir, alinear y sostener un estándar sin autoridad formal sobre las personas con las que trabajas.
Buscamos a un/a ingeniero/a de software fullstack con harta experiencia, para:
Entender el onboarding de punta a punta. Qué rol cumple cada paso, por qué existe, quién es su usuario, qué producto lo necesita y qué pasa cuando falla. Hoy ese mapa completo no vive en la cabeza de nadie.
Mejorar la experiencia de hoy desde el primer mes. Antes de que exista una sola línea de código de la reescritura ya hay mucho por ganar: ver dónde se traba la gente, atacar los pasos que más fricción generan y liberar mejoras sobre el proceso que ya está andando.
Diseñar y liderar la reescritura. Proponer la arquitectura del onboarding definitivo: pasos como piezas componibles, con sus actores, precondiciones, estados y vigencia explícitos, en vez de pantallas encadenadas. Que sea mantenible, evolucionable y que minimice errores por construcción.
Decidir qué se reutiliza entre productos. Si alguien ya completó un paso para contratar un producto, ¿se lo volvemos a pedir para el siguiente? Reutilizar baja la fricción; repetir sostiene la cobertura de riesgo. Esa discusión se lleva con Riesgo y con Producto: no la define ingeniería sola.
Construir para el Maxxa internacional. Esta reescritura es la versión que se lleva a los otros países. Los conceptos se repiten —identidad, cobro automático, firma, garantías— pero el proveedor y la regulación cambian en cada mercado.
Coordinar sin mandar. Buena parte de los servicios que el onboarding orquesta los construyen otros equipos de Tecnología. No los diriges: los alineas, con una visión global de lo que tu producto tiene que lograr y con un estándar alto de lo que aceptas.
Arquitectura hexagonal / puertos y adaptadores, o Clean Architecture aplicada al frontend , con separación real entre dominio, casos de uso e infraestructura. Es a donde queremos llegar con la reescritura: si ya lo hiciste, mejor; si no, es parte de lo que vas a aprender acá.
Python en profundidad (Django/Flask/FastAPI) o experiencia sólida en otro backend.
Haber sido referente técnico de frontend de un equipo: no solo escribir buen código, sino haber subido el piso de los demás.
Sensibilidad de UX y accesibilidad ; experiencia leyendo métricas de interacción y experimentación (Mixpanel, Amplitude o similares).
Uso fluido de herramientas de IA para desarrollo (Claude Code, Cursor) y estándares como MCP.
Formación en Ingeniería Civil en Computación / Informática, Industrial mención TI/Computación o afines. No es excluyente.
Cómo trabajamos este rol. Reportas al Tech Lead de Experiencia Unificada, el equipo dueño de login, registro, home, perfil y ahora onboarding. No tienes personas a cargo: tu peso en la organización viene de ser dueño/a del onboarding y de coordinarte con los equipos que construyen los servicios que ese proceso orquesta.

Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

As a Software Engineer on ML Platform at Cursor, you'll build the infrastructure that turns real product usage into better models — and keeps research moving fast on large GPU fleets. ML Platform is organized into four teams. Depending on your background, you may join any of them:
Telemetry — Own the collection and serving path that turns real product use into a record research can trust; without slowing the product, and under a small, explicit policy. Client-side or high-volume ingestion experience is a plus.
ML Data Platform — Build the shared environments and pipeline substrate researchers extend, so new experiments don’t fork their own stack.
Observability — Make it easy for researchers to start, watch, and debug their own runs.
ML DevX and Systems — Shorten the path from idea to a trusted run on the research fleet.
We're looking for strong distributed-systems and infrastructure engineers who want to sit next to research and ship platform primitives that move the product.
We're in-person with cozy offices in North Beach, San Francisco, Palo Alto, and Manhattan, New York, complete with well-stocked libraries.

Design, build, and operate core platform systems used daily by ML researchers and product engineers
Partner closely with research to turn recurring pain into durable infrastructure
Own reliability, performance, and developer experience for the systems in your lane
Ship iteratively in a flat, high-ownership environment. Measure impact, then raise the bar
You may be a fit if
You have a strong background in systems / infrastructure software engineering and enjoy building platforms other engineers depend on
You've owned production distributed systems at meaningful scale (ingestion, data pipelines, scheduling/orchestration, or similar)
You're comfortable across Linux, cloud and/or bare metal, and modern orchestration (Kubernetes, Ray, or equivalent)
You like working closely with ML researchers and product engineers
You thrive where ownership is high and the feedback loop is short
Especially strong backgrounds by team
Telemetry: event ingestion, product analytics pipelines, OpenTelemetry / tracing, reliable data APIs
Product Data Platform: data frameworks, Spark / Flink / Ray, ML dataset and training-data infrastructure
Observability: experiment / run monitoring, debug and eval tooling, agent-friendly observability UX
ML DevX and Systems: GPU / cluster scheduling, job queues, node health, research compute developer experience
Applying
If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

Join the Sleep Fitness Movement
At Eight Sleep, we're on a mission to fuel human potential through optimal sleep. As the world's first sleep fitness company, we're redefining what it means to be well-rested and building the most advanced hardware, software, and AI technology to make it possible. Our products power peak mental, physical, and emotional performance by transforming every night of sleep into a personalized, data-driven recovery experience.
Every role at Eight Sleep is a chance to create cutting-edge technology, collaborate with world-class talent, and help shape a future where sleep isn't passive, it's a powerful tool for living better. If you're tired of the ordinary and driven to build at the edge of what's possible, this is your moment.
High Standards. No Apologies.
We operate with intensity because our mission demands it. At Eight Sleep, we bring the same mindset as the world's top performers: focused, relentless, and always pushing to be in the top 1% of our craft. This isn't a 9-to-5. Our team is deeply committed, often putting in the extra effort, not because we're told to, but because we're invested in building something category-defining.

We're hiring a Frontend Web Developer Engineer to help us move fast on eightsleep.com . You'll work closely with the growth, marketing, and design teams to ship landing pages, run a high volume of A/B tests, and keep our analytics and conversion funnels sharp on a high-traffic storefront serving customers around the world.
This is a hands-on, high-velocity role. If you like turning ideas into shipped, measurable experiments, and seeing your work go live within days, you'll feel at home here.
How you’ll contribute
Build marketing pages. Ship landing pages, campaign pages, and partner/influencer pages, translating designs into clean, responsive, accessible components.
Run experiments end-to-end. Design, build, and launch A/B tests; instrument the funnels you need, then read the results and share what you learn. Bring your own test ideas to the table.
Build scalable, templatized systems that make launching new pages efficient and consistent.
Own the analytics stack. Maintain and extend our tracking and advertising integrations, and keep event data accurate and privacy-compliant.
Optimize conversion. Improve every step of the funnel: promos, email capture, CTAs, messaging, and page performance.
Own SEO and accessibility. Keep metadata, sitemaps, structured data, and page speed in great shape, and make sure everything you ship is accessible.
Build for a global audience. Create localized pages and experiments across our supported regions and languages.
What you need to succeed
Strong React and Next.js experience; comfortable across the modern front-end stack and TypeScript.
Experiment-design sense .You can frame a clean hypothesis, think about sample size and significance, and trust a result before acting on it.
5+ years in front-end web development , ideally in growth, marketing, or ecommerce contexts.
Strong attention to detail. You QA your own work and ship things that don't bounce back.
Hands-on with product analytics (Amplitude or similar): funnels, cohorts, and event tracking.
Comfortable with Google Tag Manager and GA4 .
Care for web performance (Core Web Vitals) and accessibility .
Awareness of data privacy / consent requirements and how they affect tracking.
AI built into how you work. You use coding assistants and other AI tools to move faster and raise your output.
A bias toward shipping quickly and iterating.

Experience with SEO/AEO, including structured data.
Internationalization / localization work.
Server-side conversion tracking (CAPI / server-to-server).
Tailwind CSS and design-system component work; Figma-to-code workflows.
Familiarity with a headless CMS and media/asset pipelines.
Experience with media-heavy sites and asset optimization.
How we work
Config-driven and fast. A lot of our growth surface is defined declaratively, so a well-scoped change goes from idea to production in a day, not a sprint. We're experiment-led, we'd rather ship a test and learn than debate. You'll have real ownership over what you build and a direct line to the impact it has.

The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.
So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff.

Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place.

Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.
Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. Every engineer at Flexport ships code that moves real freight across 112 countries. The faster , more reliable and safer they can do that, the faster the world's supply chains move. The PSI (Platform, Security & Infrastructure) team makes this possible: we build and operate the infrastructure and foundations that hundreds of engineers rely on to run Flexport’s products around the clock.
This is not a role where you wait for tickets. You'll look across systems, identify risks before they become incidents, and work with the software engineering and security teams to make our infrastructure more resilient, observable, efficient, secure, and easier to operate.

Designing, building and operating reliable, scalable infrastructure in AWS and other cloud platforms

Evolving our observability stack (Openmetrics, Datadog) to make insights into our systems as good and easy to understand as possible.
Setting standards for our Infrastructure-as-Code codebases (Terraform)
Creating and supporting developers with CI/CD pipelines (Buildkit, Github Actions), build tooling (Gradle, Bazel, npm/pnpm/bun, Go and Cargo) and artifact repositories (Artifactory, ECR, github)
Improving our incident response tooling to ensure we can efficiently handle incidents when they occur
Crossing organizational boundaries to align with product teams and ship changes that impact the whole engineering org

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.
Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

s.h: SENIOR NETWORK SOFTWARE ENGINEER I/II - SECRET CLEARANCE
s.t:

Knowledge of secure network systems is a must have, with RF and spacecraft experience being an additional benefit. This role will report to the Head of Flight Software.

Manage suppliers and subcontractors to successfully develop and test an integrated system

Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale.

More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP.

While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches.

Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet.

We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.
Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own.

Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

Stripe is large enough that individual products and projects can be rapidly deployed to a meaningful fraction of the world’s businesses, but small enough that individual agency still has outsized impact. Small teams can impact how millions of businesses grow. Right now the global economy is replatforming around AI, creating new opportunities for growth. We’re at the center of this, and we think the best work is still in front of us.
To meet this moment, we’re looking for people who move with urgency, like hard problems, and want their work to matter at a time of great change. If that’s you, there’s no better place to build your career.

Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before.
Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.

About Supabase
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

We’re building a high-performance CI/CD execution platform similar to runners used by tools like Buildkite, GitHub Actions, and Blacksmith CI. Our platform executes developer pipelines reliably at scale, integrates deeply with source control, and automates build, test, and deployment workflows.
In this role, you will design and build the distributed systems responsible for running CI/CD pipelines securely and efficiently. This includes orchestrating ephemeral compute environments, managing build isolation, scheduling jobs across fleets of workers, and ensuring reliability at scale.
This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.
What You’ll Be Responsible For
Design and improve the core orchestration engine that manages the lifecycle of creating, merging, and rebasing Supabase Branches .
Provision ephemeral sandboxed execution environment on EKS / ECS for running untrusted build workloads from connected git repositories with securely managed secrets.
Implement job scheduling that scale to thousands of concurrent builds.
Optimize and reduce pipeline runtimes with caching, artifact storage, and dependency reuse.
Manage retry, timeout, cancellation, and failure-propagation logic to ensure pipelines behave predictably under failure conditions.
Instrument the full pipeline lifecycle with observability tooling to surface traces, metrics, and structured logs to the end user.
Develop configuration files (JSON / TOML) and integrations (Terraform / Pulumi) that allow teams to easily define, trigger, and inspect pipelines in code.
You Might Be a Good Fit If You
Have strong software engineering skills (Go and Typescript required);
Have 3+ years of experience building and operating cloud infrastructure or distributed systems at scale;
Have cloud Infrastructure knowledge - familiarity with AWS constructs is required, past experience using the AWS SDKs and IaC tools (Pulumi, Terraform, etc) to build and operate infrastructure is strongly preferred.
Have a production operations mindset - track record of building reliable, observable, and maintainable systems
Have an ownership mindset - you thrive in being able to operate independently with high-level guidance
Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences
Have experience in async or globally distributed teams
Are energized by solving real-world problems for developers
Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving quickly

Fully Remote
We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.
Tech Allowance
Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.
Annual Off-Sites
Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.
Flexible Work
We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.
Professional Development
Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

A rigorous problem-solver who instinctively verifies assumptions rather than guessing — you dig into logs, code, and system behavior before proposing a fix, and you're comfortable being wrong in public if it gets the team to the right answer faster.

Fluent with AI as a working tool, not a crutch — you use it to move faster through exploration, boilerplate, and first drafts, but you still own the correctness of what ships, and you can tell the difference between "the model sounds confident" and "this is actually verified."
Someone who treats AI-assisted output the same way you'd treat a junior engineer's PR — useful, often good, but reviewed with the same rigor as anything else before it touches production.
A mentor who multiplies the team's effectiveness, not just your own — you review code like you're teaching, you pair when it helps someone level up, and you measure your impact partly by how the engineers around you grow.
Someone who leaves things better than you found them: documentation, test coverage, runbooks, and team practices all improve because you touched them.
Low-ego and high-trust — you can disagree strongly in a design review and still buy the team a round after it's decided.
A pleasure to work with — even at 2am during an incident.

* Beratung der Fachbereiche, Koordination externer Partner und Mitarbeit in Projekten und Fachgremien

* Höhere Ausbildung in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder Betriebswirtschaft beziehungsweise eine vergleichbare Qualifikation
